note: Normal daily run, Friday 11 Sep 2026 ~07:02-07:45 SGT. As of the Thu 10 Sep US close / pre-Asia-open (HK/SG also closed 10 Sep; JP/KR index data consolidates a session late). Thursday was a hot-PPI risk-off day with three genuinely distinct, decoupled catalysts hitting different parts of the book on the same session -- see items below.

items.headline: August PPI runs hot on annual terms, pushing Sep 15-16 Fed hike odds from ~60% to ~70%
items.summary: Headline PPI was in line on the closely-watched monthly figure (+0.4% m/m, matching consensus) but ran hot on annual/core terms (+5.4% y/y, ~0.1pt above consensus; core +0.3% m/m/+4.7% y/y), with over three-quarters of the gain traced to final-demand energy -- diesel alone +24.1% m/m. CME FedWatch hike odds for the Sep 15-16 FOMC jumped to roughly 70% (dispersion 48-70% across trackers through the session).
items.actionable: Raises the odds of a real hike (not just a hold) at next week's FOMC -- the levered silver/gold-miners sleeve and the S-REIT book both face a genuine rate headwind if today's CPI confirms the hawkish repricing.

items.headline: Gold and silver miners routed on the real-yield reaction -- SLV -5.3%, Barrick -7% -- even as the Hormuz haven case stays intact
items.summary: SLV fell 5.30% to $57.50, GLD -1.73% to $396.36, GDX -3.46%, with single names hit harder still (Barrick -6.99%, First Majestic -4.86%, Hecla -3.98%, Pan American -4.25%). Kitco described the tape as metals 'trading as a rates-and-dollar market, not a clean safe-haven market' right now, compounding profit-taking after gold's push to 10-week highs. The technical read is disputed: one recap shows gold/silver closing below both 50- and 200-DMA with RSI ~29-31 (oversold/reversal-leaning); other coverage frames it as a pullback before an expected Q4 rally.
items.actionable: The single biggest one-day hit to the levered silver/gold-miners sleeve in weeks -- today's CPI print is the near-term tell for whether this is a scare to buy or the start of a deeper reversal.

items.headline: Hormuz war escalates to its largest attack wave yet -- Iran claims strikes on 10 vessels, oil pushes toward $109
items.summary: Iran claimed strikes on 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz overnight into 10 Sep -- described in coverage as the largest declared wave of shipping attacks since the war began. The US is retaliating under a new 'tanker-for-tanker' policy after disabling or destroying five Iranian tankers over the prior days; CENTCOM's commander said 'if you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost.' Brent pushed toward $108-109 intraday and WTI past $103.88, even as gold sold off the SAME session -- a clean decoupling of the real-yield trade from the physical-supply-risk trade.
items.actionable: This is a genuinely worsening, not fading, conflict -- supportive of maintaining the cash pile and energy exposure as hedges, and a real cost headwind via energy prices for the broader portfolio even as it no longer reliably lifts gold/silver on the same session.

items.headline: Rare-earth basket sells off on Trump-Xi summit thaw hopes -- MP -5.5%, USA Rare Earth -4%, REMX -5%
items.summary: Reports that a Trump-Xi summit could be scheduled in Washington later in September, seen as extending last year's trade truce, hit the ex-China rare-earth basket: USA Rare Earth -4% to $16.36, MP Materials -5.49% to $51.32, Critical Metals Corp -2%, REMX -5%, Energy Fuels -6.32%, Lynas -2.71%. The logic per coverage: 'any sign that the two capitals are moving toward a durable arrangement removes part of the reason to pay a premium for a Western substitute.' This happened the SAME day USA Rare Earth broke ground on a $1.2bn South Carolina magnet facility, and China's actual export-control posture has not visibly eased.
items.actionable: A distinct catalyst from the same-day metals rout -- the watchlist thesis (China controls ~70% of mining, ~90% of processing) is unchanged by summit optimism alone; the 24 Sep Xi visit remains the real binary catalyst, and today's move could reverse sharply on the actual outcome.

items.headline: August CPI due today -- the decisive print before next week's FOMC
items.summary: US CPI for August releases today (11 Sep, 8:30am ET), with consensus at 3.4% y/y headline and 2.4% y/y core. Following yesterday's hot-on-annual PPI, this is the print markets are watching to confirm or walk back the jump in Sep 15-16 hike odds to ~70%.
items.actionable: The single biggest near-term catalyst for the whole book today -- a hot print would cement hike odds and extend pressure on gold/silver and S-REITs; a soft print could quickly revive the dip-buying case in the metals sleeve given how oversold it now looks technically.

items.headline: CNN Fear & Greed falls further to 33/Fear as crypto sentiment rises to 69/Greed -- a widening divergence
items.summary: CNN's live Fear & Greed Index fell to 33 (Fear) as of the Thu 10 Sep 6:45pm ET reading, down from 38 the prior close and 47 a week ago, driven by the hot-PPI-triggered selloff and VIX's 8.38% spike to 17.84. The dedicated crypto Fear & Greed Index (alternative.me) moved the opposite direction, rising to 69 (Greed) from 66 the prior day -- widening rather than narrowing the equity/crypto sentiment gap.
items.actionable: Equity fear deepening while crypto stays complacent reads as a divergence worth treating with caution, not as a contrarian buy signal in either asset, heading into today's CPI and the Sep 15 CLARITY Act vote.

items.headline: USA Rare Earth breaks ground on $1.2bn South Carolina magnet facility
items.summary: USA Rare Earth broke ground on a new $1.2bn magnet manufacturing facility in South Carolina, a concrete step in the DoD-adjacent ex-China rare-earth buildout -- announced the same week the stock fell on unrelated Trump-Xi summit thaw-hope sentiment (see above).
items.actionable: A genuine fundamental positive for the ex-China rare-earth thesis that was overridden by macro-diplomatic sentiment this week -- worth distinguishing company execution (on track) from the summit-driven price action.

items.headline: Congress: Rep. McGuire's Aug 18 trade corrected to an NVDA buy (not sell) alongside an AAPL sell; Rep. Fields discloses new Apple buy
items.summary: A Benzinga report dated 9 Sep clarifies Rep. John McGuire's (R-VA) 18 Aug trades as a NVIDIA BUY paired with an Apple SELL -- correcting this file's prior record, which had both legs as sells -- filed roughly 2 weeks before Apple's Sept 1 CEO transition. Separately, Rep. Cleo Fields (D-LA) disclosed a new Apple buy ($1,001-$15,000, transacted 13 Aug, filed 2 Sep), part of a pattern of recurring Magnificent-Seven-adjacent purchases through 2026.
items.actionable: Routine congressional portfolio activity in mega-cap tech; the McGuire correction is a data-accuracy note rather than a trading signal.

items.headline: KOSPI's first-ever close above 7,000 reverses on quadruple-witching foreign selling
items.summary: Korea's KOSPI closed above 7,000 for the first time ever on 9 Sep (+1.40% to 7,051.64) on genuine foreign and institutional buying, before reversing on Thursday's quadruple-witching session (-0.25% to 7,033.92) as foreigners sold roughly ₩2.7 trillion, with retail alone defending the 7,000 level.
items.actionable: The 4-9 Sep rally looked like genuine chip-sector demand, not a buyback-only move, but Thursday's foreign outflow with retail as the sole buyer is a fragility flag worth watching for the owner's HK-tech-adjacent semiconductor exposure.

items.headline: Southbound Stock Connect keeps buying the HK tech dip through a 5th straight session
items.summary: Mainland money bought HK$4.55bn of Hong Kong stocks via Southbound Stock Connect on 10 Sep even as the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 2.04% (Zhipu AI -10%+) -- the 5th consecutive net-buying session since a 4 Sep sell shock, extending a dip-buying rather than capitulation pattern through this week's macro-driven volatility.
items.actionable: Mainland conviction in HK tech looks intact through the shared global (Fed/oil/yields) drawdown -- a mildly reassuring signal for the owner's Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi book even as the sector corrects.

items.headline: Dollar falls a 4th straight session despite rising Fed hike odds -- an unreconciled counter-signal
items.summary: DXY declined for a fourth consecutive session on 10 Sep even as Sep 15-16 hike odds rose to roughly 70% on the hot PPI print -- the opposite of the textbook rates/dollar relationship. No single source fully explained the divergence; flagged as a genuine open question rather than resolved.
items.actionable: Worth monitoring for SGX-bank and EM-adjacent exposure -- a weaker dollar alongside higher US rates is an unusual combination that hasn't been reconciled yet.

items.headline: Q3 2026 13F filing deadline confirmed for Nov 16, 2026
items.summary: The next round of super-investor 13F filings, covering the quarter ending 30 Sep 2026, are due Monday 16 Nov 2026 (the nominal 45-day deadline of 14 Nov falls on a Saturday). No new 13D/13G filings were found this run for any of the ten tracked funds (Berkshire, Soros, Duquesne, Pershing Square, Bridgewater, Scion, Appaloosa, Tiger Global, Gates Foundation Trust).
items.actionable: A calendar marker, not an actionable trade -- the next real whale-positioning update is roughly two months out.
